documents.content:
Purchase requisitions

A department manager approves requisitions up to ten thousand dollars. Larger requests also require finance approval. Every requisition states the business purpose, cost center and requested delivery date.

Purchase orders

A procurement officer converts an approved requisition into a purchase order. Orders above fifty thousand dollars require the procurement director's signature before they are sent to a supplier.

Supplier onboarding

New suppliers provide tax registration, banking evidence and a signed code of conduct. Compliance screens sanctions before procurement activates the supplier record.

Supplier payment

Accounts payable releases payment after matching the purchase order, receipt and invoice. Bank-detail changes require callback verification using the supplier's previously registered phone number.

Goods receipt

Warehouse staff count delivered units and record visible damage before accepting a shipment. Quantity differences are placed on receipt hold and reported to the buyer.

Invoice disputes

Accounts payable sends price or tax discrepancies to the buyer within two business days. The disputed amount remains blocked until procurement documents a resolution.

Inventory cycle counts

High-value items are counted monthly and ordinary stock quarterly. A variance above two percent triggers a recount by a different employee and review by inventory control.

Stock adjustments

An inventory supervisor approves adjustments below five hundred dollars. Larger adjustments require finance approval. The record includes the reason, item number and supporting count sheet.

Return to supplier

Quality authorizes a supplier return after documenting the defect. Warehouse staff isolate the material and procurement obtains a return number before shipment.

Customer returns

Customer service issues a return authorization within thirty days of delivery. Warehouse staff inspect the returned product, and finance processes an approved credit within five business days.

Sole-source purchases

A requester documents why competition is unavailable. The department head and procurement director approve the justification before an order is created. Price reasonableness must still be recorded.

Competitive bidding

Purchases above twenty-five thousand dollars require at least three written bids unless an approved exception applies. Procurement records the evaluation criteria and award decision.

Obsolete inventory

Inventory control identifies stock with no demand for twelve months. The department owner chooses transfer, sale or disposal. Destruction requires signatures from inventory control and finance.

Emergency purchasing

An emergency order may proceed to protect people, property or essential operations. The duty manager gives verbal approval, and the requester submits written justification within one business day.
